title.pinyin: Tā shì bu shì shēng bìng le

instruction.hanzi: 读一读，说说这些词语是什么意思。
instruction.english: Read the words and phrases aloud and say what they mean.

items.english: to get up in the morning
every day
to go running
to get sick
to take medicine
to rest
very busy
to have no time

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 马克，你每天早上几点起床？
dialogue.pinyin: Mǎkè, nǐ měi tiān zǎoshang jǐ diǎn qǐ chuáng?
dialogue.english: Mark, what time do you get up every morning?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 六点。我每天早上都去跑步。
dialogue.pinyin: Liù diǎn. Wǒ měi tiān zǎoshang dōu qù pǎo bù.
dialogue.english: Six o'clock. I go running every morning.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ měi tiān pǎo duōshao fēnzhōng?
dialogue.english: How many minutes do you run each day?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 四十多分钟。你也和我一起去跑步吧！
dialogue.pinyin: Sìshí duō fēnzhōng. Nǐ yě hé wǒ yìqǐ qù pǎo bù ba!
dialogue.english: Forty-odd minutes. Come running with me!

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.pinyin: Liù diǎn? Tài zǎo le! Wǒ xiǎng shuì jiào.
dialogue.english: Six? That's way too early! I want to sleep.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.pinyin: Nà qī diǎn, zěnmeyàng?
dialogue.english: Then how about seven?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.pinyin: Hǎo ba.
dialogue.english: OK, fine.

newWords.english: to get up, to get out of bed

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 王明，马克今天没来。他是不是生病了？
dialogue.pinyin: Wáng Míng, Mǎkè jīntiān méi lái. Tā shì bu shì shēng bìng le?
dialogue.english: Wang Ming, Mark didn't come today. Is he sick?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.pinyin: Shì, tā zài yīyuàn.
dialogue.english: Yes, he's in the hospital.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.pinyin: Tā shēntǐ zěnmeyàng?
dialogue.english: How is he doing?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 不太好。医生说他要吃药，多休息。
dialogue.pinyin: Bú tài hǎo. Yīshēng shuō tā yào chī yào, duō xiūxi.
dialogue.english: Not great. The doctor says he needs to take medicine and get plenty of rest.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.pinyin: Tā shénme shíhou néng chū yuàn?
dialogue.english: When can he leave the hospital?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 我不知道。我们下午去看他吧。
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒ bù zhīdào. Wǒmen xiàwǔ qù kàn tā ba.
dialogue.english: I don't know. Let's go and see him this afternoon.

newWords.english: to fall ill, to be sick
to rest, to take a rest
to leave hospital, to be discharged

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.pinyin: Mǎkè, nǐ hǎo diǎnr le ma?
dialogue.english: Mark, are you feeling a bit better?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.pinyin: Hǎo duō le. Nǐ jīntiān bù máng ma?
dialogue.english: Much better. Aren't you busy today?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 不忙，下午我有时间。这是我给你买的水果。
dialogue.pinyin: Bù máng, xiàwǔ wǒ yǒu shíjiān. Zhè shì wǒ gěi nǐ mǎi de shuǐguǒ.
dialogue.english: No, I'm free this afternoon. Here's some fruit I bought for you.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 谢谢！你看见我的医生了吗？他很高！
dialogue.pinyin: Xièxie! Nǐ kànjiàn wǒ de yīshēng le ma? Tā hěn gāo!
dialogue.english: Thanks! Did you see my doctor? He's really tall!

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.pinyin: Kànjiàn le. Tā duō gāo?
dialogue.english: I did. How tall is he?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.pinyin: Yì mǐ jiǔ!
dialogue.english: One meter ninety!

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.pinyin: Tài gāo le!
dialogue.english: That's so tall!

title.english: Mark is out of the hospital

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.pinyin: Jīntiān wǒ chū yuàn le!
dialogue.english: I got out of the hospital today!

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 在医院的时候，我每天都吃药、睡觉。
dialogue.pinyin: Zài yīyuàn de shíhou, wǒ měi tiān dōu chī yào, shuì jiào.
dialogue.english: In the hospital, all I did every day was take medicine and sleep.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.pinyin: Xiànzài wǒ shēntǐ hǎo duō le.
dialogue.english: Now I feel much better.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒ hěn xiǎng chūqu tī zúqiú.
dialogue.english: I really want to go out and play football.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 安娜说："不能去！你要在家多休息。"
dialogue.pinyin: Ānnà shuō: "Bù néng qù! Nǐ yào zài jiā duō xiūxi."
dialogue.english: Anna says, "You can't! You need to stay home and rest."

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 好吧，那我在家看足球吧。
dialogue.pinyin: Hǎo ba, nà wǒ zài jiā kàn zúqiú ba.
dialogue.english: Fine. I'll watch football at home, then.

newWords.english: to go out, to come out

explanation.hanzi: 说话人对一件事已经有了一个猜想，想让对方确认的时候，可以用"是不是"提问。"是不是"可以放在谓语前面，也可以放在句子后面（……，是不是？）。回答用"是"或者"不是"。
explanation.english: Use 是不是 when you already have a guess and want the other person to confirm it, like "isn't it?" or "is it true that...?". It can go right before the predicate (他是不是生病了？) or be tagged onto the end of a statement (你是马克的朋友，是不是？). Answer with 是 or 不是. In pinyin, 不 is usually light here: shì bu shì.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ shì bu shì shēng bìng le?
Wáng Míng shì bu shì hěn máng?

examples.hanzi: 你是马克的朋友，是不是？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ shì Mǎkè de péngyou, shì bu shì?
Míngtiān huì xià yǔ, shì bu shì?
examples.english: It's going to rain tomorrow, isn't it?

explanation.hanzi: "每"后面一般要用量词：每个人、每本书、每个星期。"天、年"本身像量词，所以直接说"每天、每年"。有"每"的句子后面常常用"都"。
explanation.english: 每 (měi) means "every, each". Normally a measure word follows it: 每个人, 每本书, 每个星期. A few time words act as their own measure words, so they attach directly: 每天, 每年. Sentences with 每 very often add 都 before the verb: 我每天都跑步.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān zǎoshang dōu pǎo bù.

examples.hanzi: 每个学生都有一本汉语书。
examples.pinyin: Měi ge xuésheng dōu yǒu yì běn Hànyǔ shū.
examples.english: Every student has a Chinese book.

examples.hanzi: 他每个星期都去看他妈妈。
examples.pinyin: Tā měi ge xīngqī dōu qù kàn tā māma.
examples.english: He goes to see his mother every week.

title.english: 多 + Adjective as a Question (How tall? How old?)

explanation.hanzi: "多＋形容词"用来问程度，意思是"有多……"：多高、多大、多长时间。回答的时候说具体的数。
explanation.english: Put 多 (duō) before an adjective to ask "how + adjective?": 多高 "how tall", 多大 "how old / how big". The answer gives an amount: 一米七, 二十多岁. Later you'll also use 多长时间 "how long (a time)" in the same way.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ duō gāo? —— Yì mǐ qī.
examples.english: How tall are you? — One meter seventy.

examples.hanzi: 你女儿多大了？——十几岁了。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ nǚ'ér duō dà le? —— Shíjǐ suì le.
examples.english: How old is your daughter? — She's in her teens.

singleComponentChars.meaning: to grow, to be born; life
singleComponentChars.etymology: A young plant pushing up out of the ground: the bottom stroke is the earth, the rest is the sprout. From "to grow" come "to be born" and "life", and also "to get" an illness, as in 生病.
A drawing of a tall building: a pointed roof on top, a lookout room in the middle and a wide gateway at the bottom.

prompt.hanzi: 两人一组，谈谈你的一天和身体。
prompt.english: In pairs, talk about your daily routine and your health.

activities: Daily schedule: ask your partner 你每天几点起床？几点吃饭？几点睡觉？ and write down their day. Then report it to the class with 每天……都…….
Guess and check: make guesses about your partner with 是不是 (你是不是每天都跑步？你是不是很忙？) and see how many you get right.
Height line: ask 你多高？ around the group and line up from shortest to tallest, saying your height in 米.
Doctor and patient: one partner is a doctor, the other is sick. Use 身体、吃药、休息、出院 and 多 + adjective.
